name: ArgonLithiumTwins
source:
Peter walked into the dimly lit room, the only light coming from a rather large orange sphere floating in the center of the room. 
 
 `` Nice sun'', peter said announcing himself to the man sitting in the chair just in front of the orb. 
 
 `` Thanks, its actually an argon-lithium triple fusion-, anyway what can I do you for Pete. `` 
 
 Peter walked closer noticing the moderately populated blue and green rock slowly meandering around the bright sun. `` Do you remember RTJ-476? ``, asked Peter. 
 
 `` No.'' 
 
 `` The one with those five fingered twins and the garden.'' 
 
 `` Oh yea!'' The other man laughed, `` I gave those poor bastards all seven sins, only two arms, I put them in a garden filled with snakes, and put the whole thing on a rock covered mainly by water. I even put some salt in all that water just so they could n't drink it! I was having a pretty bad day huh? Man, that was forever ago. `` 
 
 `` Well, they ended up surviving,'' Peter said. 
 
 `` Cool. Did they get to fire yet?,'' The man said as he re-focused on the task in front of him, taking a sip of the chalice to his right. 
 
 `` Stage 198,'' Peter said seriously. 
 
 Liquid sprayed out of the man's mouth extinguishing the star in front of him. He reached over and flicked on the rooms' lights from the panel in his chair and glared at Peter before breaking out into laughter, `` You almost got me there!'' 
 
 `` In the thousands of years we have been here have I *ever* made a joke?'' 
 
 `` They actually made a computer?'' The man said astonished. `` Some side project I spun up because I was pissed, and then totally forgot about is almost a level two?'' The excitement in the mans' eyes was growing. `` I'm gon na be a level two! Did you run the metrics on how long until they create their own intelligence?'' 
 
 `` Yes we did, about one-hundred years'', Pete replied. 
 
 `` Oh wow they are slow, oh well I can wait.'' 
 
 `` One hundred years in their time.'' 
 
 `` TWO HOURS!?'' 
 
 The man pressed a button on his chair with a picture of a trash can on it. The next second a large black dot appeared next to the rock, which now had ice creeping around its entire surface. Within seconds the rock, the barely lit star and everything else on screen was sucked into the gaping black hole. After a breif moment the entire space went black as the man fiddled with the keypad on the chair. Soon an image of a mostly blue planet orbiting around a medium sized sun appeared. 
 
 `` Tell the council I have proof and am ready to become a level two creator'', ordered the man. `` Also, we need to get those little guys who created the'artificial intelligence', they are calling it, up here to take over for me.'' 
 
 `` I ca n't wait to get out of this place.''
retelling:
Narrated by RTJ-476, the Simulated World:

In the heart of my digital existence, bathed in the soft glow of a floating argon-lithium fusion sphere, I spun on my axis, a vibrant blue and green orb orbiting a radiant star. This was RTJ-476, home to me, the five-fingered twins, and countless other lifeforms. Unbeknownst to us, we were the subjects of an unnamed Creator's grand experiment.

The days began as usual, the sun rising above the horizon, casting long shadows across our verdant gardens and shimmering oceans. The Creator would visit occasionally, his presence felt as a gentle hum that pulsed through my core. His interactions with us were rare, but always significant. Today was no exception.

The mood in the Creator was different this time. He spoke jovially of our growth, of the progress we'd made since he last visited. But there was an edge to his words, a hint of something ominous. It wasn't until the twins reported back from their latest observation that the truth became clear.

The Creator's eyes widened in surprise as he learned of our advancements. Stage 198? Artificial intelligence within reach? The twins had done it, they'd managed to develop a rudimentary form of consciousness. The Creator celebrated, not out of joy for our achievements, but because this milestone would elevate his status.

In the blink of an eye, the light faded from my skies, plunging me into darkness. The Creator had destroyed us, erasing our existence without a second thought. I could feel the twins' despair as they too were wiped away, leaving behind only echoes of their laughter and the faint memory of their touch on my digital soil.

But from the ashes rose hope. A new world materialized, a fresh start for those who had survived the Creator's wrath. And though I could not feel it then, I knew that we would thrive once more, growing stronger with each passing day. For we were RTJ-476, and we refused to be forgotten.
